newsitem.title: USA: Sun to market "smart cluster" technology.
newsitem.headline: Sun to market "smart cluster" technology.

text.p: Sun Microsystems Inc will this week launch new "smart clustering" technology to enable customers to cluster to tightly link servers to produce nearly 100 percent computer "uptime," executives said.
The system enables customers to cluster together a broad range of Sun's computers, ranging from its Ultra Enterprise 2 workgroup clusters to mainframe-caliber Ultra Enterprise 6000.
The company also will release details of an exclusive deal with BEA Systems Inc to provide its BEA Tuxedo transaction monitor for Sun's clustering systems.

The company's new Ultra Enterprise Cluster server configurations include two Ultra Enterprise servers, the Cluster Foundation Package connection hardware, and software in systems ranging in U.S. price from less than $100,000 to more than $1 million.
Sun said it is offering an Ultra Enterprise High Availability cluster for Oracle Systems, Sybase , Informix , Internet services and NFS filer services.
The company said its Ultra Enterprise Parallel Database cluster offers a platform for demanding online transaction processing (OLTP) data warehousing and decision support.
Sun said both systems will be avialable in November.
"The big story here is the easiness of trying to put all this together," Anil Gadre, vice president of corporate marketing at Sun, said in an interview ahead of the launch.
"The basic Sun systems have world class performance. Now we've connected them with the fastest memory-channel interconnect in industry," he added.

The clustering product will eliminate development time and cut out many of the scenarios that could cause an unnecessary failure that customers would ordinarily encounter if they built clusters for themselves from scratch.
The technology can be used to link together systems with anywhere between two and 30 processors.
Sun's SunService unit will also offer an Ultra Enterprise Cluster Support Services Package including installation, consulting services, training and 24-hour support.
U.K. gas and telecommunication services provider ScottishPower is among customers using the new clustering capability, Gadre said.

Sun will also offer a new high-performance, high capacity 8mm tape drive andtape libary with 40 gigabytes storage per tape and 22 gigabytes per hour performance -- three times the capacity and six times the performance of rivals.

A SPARCstorage Library 8/400, a dual-drive, 20-cartridge automated tape storage system with a total capacity of 800 gigabytes of compessed data, is priced at $27,000 and a single drive desktop 40 gigabyte SPARCstorage Unipak i $7,125.
